en.title: SAT1 crosses regional boundaries; livestock risk now depends on surveillance and vaccine matching
en.deck: Official SAT1 notifications across the Middle East, Asia and Africa, plus a November FAO-WOAH field mission in Mongolia, show a transboundary livestock risk whose economic impact depends on laboratory capacity, vaccine compatibility, animal-movement controls and regional reporting.
en.regime: SAT1 has been reported beyond its historical range; national surveillance and response capacity are uneven and the 14-country Middle East strategy is now an institutional framework.
en.key_risk: SAT1 reaches additional susceptible herds before serotype-matched prevention, laboratory confirmation and movement controls are deployed, causing localized production losses and wider temporary trade restrictions.

signal_rationale.delta: The existing corpus search found no SAT1/FMD report. New official notifications in November and the 24 November WOAH Middle East page update provide a date-specific cross-border livestock/market-access delta distinct from the 23 November AMR implementation-gap report and today's Global Macro.
signal_rationale.evidence: FAO reported a government-requested FAO-WOAH field assessment after SAT1 outbreaks in Mongolia's Bayan-Ulgii and Khovd provinces on 13 November. WOAH lists Botswana SAT1 on 17 November and Algeria SAT1 on 10 November, while Mauritius reported serotype O on 19 November; the report explicitly separates the serotypes and diseases. WOAH's 24 November Middle East page describes the regional SAT1 spread and 2026–2030 strategy.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Serotype spread across livestock jurisdictions → veterinary surveillance and laboratory confirmation → vaccine matching and movement controls → production/market-access interruptions → farm income, trade and public response costs.
signal_rationale.transmission: Infection and control measures can reduce animal productivity and restrict movement/export certification; delays and uneven reporting increase uncertainty and can widen trading-partner restrictions. Price and loss effects require country/product data and are not estimated here.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The systemic-risk thesis weakens if notifications stabilize with stable surveillance, affected zones remain contained, vaccine compatibility/coverage and veterinary capacity are verified, and trade restrictions remain short and narrowly targeted.

key_constraints: First-occurrence country notifications are not total outbreak counts or herd prevalence.
The 2026 count in the WOAH August summary is incomplete for the calendar year.
The Mongolia FAO update reports a field assessment, not a complete national incidence or loss estimate.
FMD serotype O in Mauritius and African swine fever in Nigeria are separate events from SAT1.
Vaccine compatibility is source- and region-specific; no product-level recommendation is made.
No food-price, livestock-loss or trade-loss estimate is calculated without affected herd, output and product-level trade data.

producer_checks.comparative_corpus: GitHub repository search found no SAT1/FMD article in the indexed corpus; existing AMR and Bundibugyo items are distinct and not duplicated.
producer_checks.novelty_decision: One date-specific thematic report selected after Global Macro; new official November notifications and regional update support a distinct animal-health, production and trade-governance delta.

visual_evidence.chart_semantics: Chart 1 compares country counts in three distinct notification categories, not a continuous time series: first occurrences in 2025, first occurrences through 26 Aug 2026, and renewed notifications after about 60 years in 2025–26. Chart 2 is the FAO qualitative risk matrix aggregation using data through 23 Feb 2026.

source_audit.citation_audit: References 1 through 8 are individually cited in both EN and PT-BR bodies. Reference 8 adds WOAH's general FMD disease overview for serotype-specific immunity; the FAO February assessment chart aggregates the likelihood totals in Table 1 and is explicitly dated and non-probabilistic.
source_audit.fao_risk_distribution: FAO rapid risk assessment v2, data through 23 Feb 2026, Table 1: among 17 unaffected countries/territories, likelihood-impact combinations sum to 2 unlikely (2 low impact), 9 likely (3 low, 4 moderate, 2 severe) and 6 very likely (2 moderate, 4 severe). The chart aggregates likelihood row totals only; these are qualitative expert categories for the following three months, not probabilities or observed cases.

manual_preflight.repository_script_validator: Candidate-specific visual grammar and depth thresholds checked against scripts/validate-editorial-depth.mjs and scripts/lib/visuals.mjs; exact-HEAD CI remains independent.

revision_reason: Clarifies the first chart and table as country-level notification categories, separating first occurrences from renewed notifications; dates the FAO assessment chart by its 23 February 2026 data vintage. No numerical values or source observations changed.
revision_scope: Presentation semantics only. EN/PT-BR table headers, first-chart title/unit/category labels and second-chart title now distinguish notification types and the FAO assessment's data cutoff without changing any series, source or thesis.
contrary_evidence: The FAO risk assessment is based on information through 23 February 2026 and its three-month horizon is historical; it cannot establish current November exposure probabilities.
Country-level WAHIS notifications do not establish herd-level prevalence, national incidence or total outbreaks.
The Middle East 2026–2030 strategy launch does not prove national funding, implementation or outcomes.
The cited FAO vaccine warning is specific to products and regions discussed in that update; it is not generalized to every vaccine or country.
limitations: No comparable country-level herd, production, bilateral livestock-trade or restriction-duration dataset supports a regional economic-loss estimate.
The 2026 first-occurrence count is through 26 August and is not a complete year-end total.
The FAO likelihood categories are expert assessments for a dated three-month horizon, not probabilities or observed infections.
Mongolia's cited field update does not provide a complete national incidence or loss series.
The 14-country regional strategy is a coordination framework; national budgets and implementation remain to be measured.
The general WOAH disease overview was accessed during revision after the stated information cutoff but adds no dated event observation.

qa_rework.changes: Revision 3 repaired the bilingual Markdown table, added a second sourced chart and a relevant WOAH source. Revision 4 clarified first-occurrence versus renewed-notification categories and dated the FAO risk-assessment chart to its 23 February 2026 data vintage; no numerical observations changed in revision 4.
